newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end higher on tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end higher on tax payments.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed higher on Monday due to caution before an expected spurt of income tax payments this week, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.339 percent against Thursday's 6.173 close, with 30-day commercial paper rising to 6.25-6.35 percent against 6.10-6.15.
The market was closed for holidays on Friday and Saturday.
Dealers said the uptrend was limited by the maturation of T$3 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit.
Another T$5 billion NCDs are scheduled to mature on Wednesday, followed by T$8 billion on Thursday and T$5 billion on Saturday.
Government bonds fell on news that Taiwan's consumer price index rose just 1.09 percent in March -- well below economists' expectations.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0900-0910 percent against 6.0940.
